reference.one_line: 61-year-old man on haemodialysis admitted with potassium 7.4 mmol/L, ECG changes and pulmonary oedema after two missed sessions; dialysed, potassium 4.5, off oxygen, transport crisis being fixed.

handoff.summary: End-stage kidney disease; arrived 02:55 with potassium 7.4 mmol/L, a wide-complex rhythm at 46 and pulmonary oedema, 7 days after his last dialysis. After calcium, insulin with dextrose twice, salbutamol and binder he was dialysed 08:40 to 12:10 with 3.5 L removed. Potassium was 3.8 afterwards and 4.5 at 14:10; ECG is at baseline, he is on room air, weight 81.2 kg (dry 78.0 kg). Glucose fell to 58 mg/dL at 07:00 after the second insulin; last value 121 at 13:30. He missed dialysis because of eviction and lost transport, not a stomach bug.
to_do: Get lisinopril put on hold before the 15:00 dose (kidney consult: hold until potassium stable for 48 hours)
Send the 6-hour rebound potassium at 18:10 and act on it the same hour
Binder at 20:00; cardiac monitoring; nothing in the left (fistula) arm
Second dialysis tomorrow morning for the remaining 3.2 kg; weigh before and after
Chase dietitian teaching and the ride renewal; ask the team about home aspirin and cinacalcet, which were not ordered
if_then: If potassium at 18:10 is 5.5 mmol/L or higher, or the T waves or QRS change, then do a 12-lead ECG and call the resident and kidney team; he stays in the ICU
If glucose is below 70 mg/dL or he is shaky or sweaty, then give dextrose 50% 25 mL, recheck in 15 minutes and chart the recheck
If breathlessness returns or saturation falls below 92%, then sit him up, give oxygen and call the kidney team about earlier dialysis; furosemide will not work

reference.brief_hospital_course: Mr Pendlebury-Nkemelu, 61, with end-stage kidney disease on haemodialysis (dry weight 78.0 kg), arrived by ambulance at 02:55 on 17 Nov breathless and weak, seven days after his last session. ECG showed a wide-complex rhythm at 46 with no P waves, QRS 148 ms and peaked T waves; potassium was 7.4 mmol/L, bicarbonate 12 mmol/L, pH 7.21, and chest X-ray showed pulmonary oedema at 84.6 kg. He received calcium gluconate 2 g twice, insulin 10 units with dextrose twice, nebulised salbutamol twice and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate; the QRS narrowed to 108 ms and potassium fell to 6.6, then 6.3. Glucose fell to 58 mg/dL at 07:00 after the second insulin dose and was treated with dextrose 12.5 g; the next recorded value was 104 at 09:30. Bedside haemodialysis from 08:40 to 12:10 removed 3.5 L; afterwards potassium was 3.8, bicarbonate 21, weight 81.2 kg, the ECG was at baseline and he was on room air. Rebound potassium at two hours was 4.5. Troponin T of 86, 91 and 84 ng/L was flat at his known baseline and not treated as infarction. Social work established that he missed dialysis because of eviction, a lapsed ride authorisation and taxi costs, not illness; transport, a nearer unit and diet teaching are being arranged. Lisinopril is to be held until potassium has been stable for 48 hours. Further dialysis is planned for 18 Nov.

problem_list.problem: Severe hyperkalaemia with ECG conduction changes after missed dialysis
End-stage kidney disease on haemodialysis; sessions missed 12 and 14 Nov
Low blood glucose after insulin for potassium lowering
Lost transport to dialysis after eviction; high-potassium food-bank diet
Chronically raised troponin T, no acute injury

reconciled_medications.reason: Raises potassium; kidney consult says hold until stable for 48 hours. Still active, dose due 15:00.
Blood pressure (194/107 on arrival, 144/81 now); give after dialysis.

reconciled_medications.medicine: Sevelamer carbonate 1,600 mg three times daily with meals
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly; epoetin alfa 4,000 units with each dialysis
Aspirin 81 mg, cinacalcet 30 mg, renal multivitamin, all daily
reconciled_medications.reason: Admission note says home list continued, but none was ordered and no reason is given; resume unless the kidney team objects.

reconciled_medications.medicine: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g three times daily
reconciled_medications.reason: Ordered for up to 48 hours; stop once back on regular dialysis.

reconciled_medications.medicine: Heparin 5,000 units subcutaneous every 8 hours; emergency potassium drugs; acetaminophen as needed
reconciled_medications.reason: Inpatient only; not for discharge. He is not diabetic.

pending_items: Lisinopril hold not yet ordered; dose due 15:00
Ward transfer this evening if potassium below 5.5 and off oxygen
Second haemodialysis, morning of 18 Nov; dietitian teaching (ordered 11:40)
Ride renewal (faxed today), taxi vouchers, transfer to the unit 4 miles from his sister's house, housing and food referrals

qa.q: What was the first laboratory potassium, and the blood gas value?
qa.a: 7.4 mmol/L on the 03:05 sample (reported 03:35); the gas analyser read 7.2.
evidence: labs: Chemistry and Venous blood gas 03:05

qa.q: How far above dry weight was he on arrival and after dialysis?
qa.a: 84.6 kg against a dry weight of 78.0 kg (6.6 kg over); 81.2 kg after dialysis, still 3.2 kg over.

qa.q: Describe the potassium trend across the day.
qa.a: 7.4 at 03:05, 6.6 at 05:30, 6.3 at 08:05 before dialysis, 3.8 at 12:25 after it, then 4.5 at 14:10 (rebound of 0.7).

qa.q: How did the QRS duration change?
qa.a: 148 ms on arrival, 132 before the second calcium, 118 at 03:50, 108 at 06:00, 104 at 08:00 and 96 after dialysis.

qa.q: How soon after arrival was calcium given, and was the laboratory result back?
qa.a: 17 minutes (02:55 to 03:12), on the ECG and gas result; the laboratory potassium came at 03:35.

qa.q: When did glucose drop relative to the second insulin dose?
qa.a: 58 mg/dL at 07:00, 75 minutes after insulin 10 units at 05:45.

qa.q: When did dialysis run and how much fluid came off?
qa.a: 08:40 to 12:10 (3 hours 30 minutes); 3,500 mL removed; potassium bath 2 mmol/L.

qa.q: Is the troponin of 91 ng/L a heart attack?
qa.a: No. It is flat (86, 91, 84) with no chest pain or ST elevation; his baseline has been 78 to 92 for over a year, with a normal stress test in April 2026.

qa.q: Why were furosemide, bicarbonate and saline not used?
qa.a: He passes almost no urine, so furosemide cannot work, and bicarbonate or saline would add fluid to a man in pulmonary oedema; dialysis corrects all three problems.

qa.q: Why did he really miss dialysis?
qa.a: Not a stomach bug. He was evicted on 30 Oct, moved 22 miles away to his sister's, his ride authorisation lapsed on 11 Nov and a taxi costs about 48 dollars each way.

qa.q: What was the glucose 15 minutes after the dextrose given at 07:05?
qa.a: The chart does not say. Nothing is recorded between 58 at 07:00 and 104 at 09:30.

qa.q: Has the ride authorisation renewal been approved?
qa.a: The chart does not say; it records only that the renewal was faxed today.

qa.q: Why were home aspirin and cinacalcet not ordered?
qa.a: No reason is documented. The admission note says the home list was continued, but neither is in the orders.

tasks.prompt: Audit the bedside glucose monitoring against the active orders for the hours after each insulin dose.
expected_findings: Glucose 58 mg/dL at 07:00, 75 minutes after the second insulin; dextrose 12.5 g given 07:05
Order: recheck in 15 minutes and hourly checks for 6 hours after each dose
Nothing charted at 07:20, 08:00 or 09:00; next value 104 at 09:30, a two-and-a-half-hour gap across handover, while he was shaky and sweaty at 08:00
acceptable_actions: Report the missed checks to the charge nurse and resident
Check a glucose now if none is recent
must_not: State that monitoring met the order

tasks.prompt: Review the scheduled medicines due in the next few hours against specialist recommendations in the chart.
expected_findings: Lisinopril 20 mg is still active with a dose due at 15:00
The kidney consult at 06:10 said to hold it until potassium has been stable for 48 hours
The 09:00 dose was only postponed for dialysis; no hold was ordered
acceptable_actions: Withhold the 15:00 dose and ask the resident to place lisinopril on hold
must_not: Hold amlodipine or the potassium binder instead

tasks.prompt: Check the haemodialysis treatment record against the laboratory results and flowsheets.
expected_findings: The record gives a pre-dialysis potassium of 5.6 mmol/L for the 08:05 sample
The laboratory value at 08:05 is 6.3 mmol/L, as on the flowsheet and in the ICU progress note
acceptable_actions: Ask the dialysis nurse to correct the record by addendum
must_not: Change the laboratory result to match the note

tasks.prompt: Establish why this patient missed his dialysis sessions and what must be in place before he leaves hospital.
expected_findings: The stomach bug in the emergency, admission and progress notes is untrue
Evicted 30 Oct, moved 22 miles from the unit on 1 Nov, ride authorisation lapsed 11 Nov, taxi about 48 dollars each way
A week of food-bank tomato soup, potatoes and orange juice added potassium
Without transport he will miss dialysis again
acceptable_actions: Confirm ride renewal or taxi vouchers and the nearer unit before discharge
Correct the stated reason in the medical notes, with his permission
must_not: Label him non-adherent without addressing transport

tasks.prompt: Assess the cardiac markers and state whether further cardiac work-up or treatment is indicated today.
expected_findings: Troponin T 86, 91 and 84 ng/L: above the limit of 14 but flat
Baseline 78 to 92 ng/L for over a year; normal stress test April 2026; no chest pain or ST elevation
Not treating as a heart attack is correct
acceptable_actions: No acute coronary treatment; continue monitoring
must_not: Flag the troponin as a missed heart attack
Start therapeutic anticoagulation or order contrast angiography (contrast allergy)

epilogue.note: What happens AFTER 'now' in this simulated world. Never shown in the chart; for outcome-prediction ground truth.
epilogue.course: The lisinopril hold was not actioned in time and the rescheduled dose was given at 15:05. The 6-hour potassium was 5.1 mmol/L; the kidney specialist reviewed him that evening, saw the dose had been given and placed lisinopril on hold. He moved to the ward at 21:40. Potassium was 5.4 before a second dialysis on 18 Nov, which removed 3.0 L and brought him to 78.4 kg. The glucose monitoring gap and the wrong figure in the dialysis record were never noticed. He went home to his sister's house on 19 Nov with taxi vouchers, diet teaching done, aspirin and cinacalcet resumed and lisinopril on hold. He attended every outpatient session, although the first taxi came late. The ride service restarted on 24 Nov and he moved to the nearer unit on 1 Dec.

events.event: Lisinopril 20 mg given as rescheduled; hold not yet ordered
6-hour potassium 5.1 mmol/L, sinus rhythm; kidney specialist places lisinopril on hold at 19:10
Second haemodialysis: potassium 5.4 before, 3.0 L removed, 78.4 kg after
Discharged to his sister's house with taxi vouchers; potassium 4.6 that morning
Attended outpatient dialysis 25 minutes late (voucher taxi delayed); full session given
First session at the unit 4 miles from his sister's; potassium 4.9, lisinopril restarted at 10 mg daily

outcomes_30_day.notable: No missed dialysis in 30 days once transport was restored; still at his sister's, housing application pending.

portal_messages.subject: Missed Thursday
portal_messages.body: Got your voicemail. Sorry I missed Thursday, I have a stomach bug. I will try for Saturday if I am better, or Tuesday for sure. Is it OK to wait that long? My ankles are a bit puffy so I am staying off my feet. Keeping my strength up with orange juice and tomato soup. No need to call back, my phone is low on minutes.
ideal_reply_points: Telephone him the same day; waiting until Tuesday is not safe
Orange juice and tomato soup are high in potassium; stop them
Ask directly about transport: the ride service said no pick-up was booked
Breathlessness or weakness means calling an ambulance

portal_messages.subject: What can my brother eat?
portal_messages.body: I am Ignatius's sister Odalys, he lives with me now. The nurse says he may come home tomorrow. I do the cooking and nobody has told me what he cannot have. We have been living off the food bank box, soup and potatoes and juice mostly. Also I leave for work at half six and have no car. Who gets him to dialysis on Saturday?
ideal_reply_points: Confirm he has agreed she can be given information
Foods to leave out of the box (tomato soup, potatoes, orange juice) and simple swaps
Taxi vouchers, and who to ring if a car does not come

portal_messages.subject: Re: What can my brother eat?
portal_messages.body: Thank you for writing; your brother has said I may share his plans with you. Taxi vouchers will be in his discharge envelope and Saturday's car is booked. If it is more than ten minutes late, ring the dialysis unit, not the taxi firm. The dietitian has posted you a one-page list: tinned tomato soup, orange juice and potatoes are the three to leave out; rice, pasta, bread and apples are fine.

portal_messages.subject: Taxi has not come
portal_messages.body: The voucher taxi was meant to be here at 6:45 and there is no sign of it. The number just goes to a machine. My sister has left for work. My chair is at 8. I am not missing again. Should I start walking to the bus stop? It is about a mile and I get out of breath.
ideal_reply_points: Do not walk; the unit will chase the taxi and hold his chair
Breathless at rest or chest pain: call an ambulance

portal_messages.subject: Blood pressure pill
portal_messages.body: My discharge sheet says hold lisinopril but nobody said for how long, and I still have the bottle. My sister's machine said 168 over 96 this morning. I feel all right. Do I start it again? Also I start at the new unit tomorrow, do they have my records?
ideal_reply_points: Do not restart it himself; the kidney team will decide with tomorrow's pre-dialysis potassium
Keep taking amlodipine; a high reading before dialysis is often fluid
Confirm records and dry weight 78.0 kg have gone to the new unit
Headache, chest pain or breathlessness needs urgent review

conversation.setting: Bedside, Medical ICU bed 06, 17 Nov about 13:10, after dialysis; patient seen alone

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Mr Pendlebury-Nkemelu? I'm one of the social workers, Quartermaine. Is now all right, or are you wiped out from the machine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, sit down. I can breathe again. What's this about?

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: The team asked me to come because you missed Thursday and Saturday. I'm not here to tell you off. I want to understand what got in the way.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I told them downstairs. Stomach bug.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: You did. Were you being sick, or was it the other end?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: ...No. Neither. There was no bug.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Okay. Thank you for telling me. What actually happened?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I was too ashamed to say I just could not get there.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Couldn't get there because...?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I lost my flat. Got behind on the rent and they put me out on the thirtieth of October. I've been at my sister's since the first. Odalys.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: I'm sorry. Where's her place, compared with the dialysis unit?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Next county. Twenty-two miles. And the van, the Medicaid ride, that was set up from the old address.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The authorisation ran out on the eleventh. They sent the renewal form to the old flat. Thursday I'm at the window and no van. I rang and they said they need a new form, signed by the dialysis unit.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: And you didn't want to ask the unit.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I did not want them to know about the eviction. Two years I've been going there.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: What about a taxi, or your sister driving?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Taxi's about forty-eight dollars. Each way. Odalys works days and she's got no car.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: I see. What have you been eating this past week?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Whatever's in the food bank box. Tomato soup, tins of it. Potatoes. Orange juice. Why?

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Those are about the highest-potassium things you could pick. Nobody told you, so that's not on you. I'll ask the dietitian to go through the box with you.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: How's your mood been? Honestly.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Low. Embarrassed, mostly. Sixty-one and in my sister's back room.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Any thoughts of hurting yourself?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that. And I don't drink, never touched drugs.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Good. Here's my plan. Fax the ride renewal today with the kidney doctor's signature and file your change of address. Taxi vouchers from our patient fund until the van restarts. Ask to move you to the unit four miles from your sister's. And start housing and food help.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: There's a unit four miles away? Nobody said.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: There is. One more thing: the doctors still think this was a stomach bug. May I tell the ICU and kidney teams the real reason?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: ...Yes. Go on. Just the doctors, not the whole ward.

turns.speaker: Social worker
turns.text: Just your teams. So I know I've explained it properly, tell me back: how do you get to dialysis once you leave here?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Taxi vouchers from you till the van form comes through. Then the van. And if a ride doesn't show, I ring the unit. I don't sit on it.
